name: nova.ui.row
signature: nova.ui.row{ count, w, h, gap, y [, x, width] } -> list of { x, y, w, h }
doc: `count` rectangles w by h in a row, `gap` apart, centred across the view (or across `width`, or starting at `x`); `y` is the top (centred when left out).

name: nova.ui.column
signature: nova.ui.column{ count, w, h, gap [, x, y] } -> list of { x, y, w, h }
doc: `count` rectangles w by h in a column, `gap` apart, centred down the view (or from `y`), at `x` (centred when left out).

name: nova.ui.hit
signature: nova.ui.hit(rect) or nova.ui.hit(x, y, w, h) -> boolean
doc: Is the pointer (the mouse, or the first finger) over the rectangle?

name: nova.ui.clicked
doc: Did the pointer go down on the rectangle in this step: a click or a tap?

name: nova.ui.choose
signature: nova.ui.choose{ rects, current [, vertical] } -> chosen, accepted, moved
doc: A choice among rectangles (cards, menu rows) by the d-pad or arrow keys (up and down with `vertical`) or the pointer: moving the pointer over one chooses it; a click on it, or A or start, accepts. `moved` says the choice changed.

name: nova.sprite
doc: Draw an image or one frame of a sprite sheet, centred on x, y, in the world layer. Options: scale, sx, sy, w, h, rotation, color, anchor, frame, and `src = { x, y, w, h }` (draw only that part of the picture, in pixels from its top left), and `shader = "shine"` with `params` and `textures` (a custom shader, shaders/shine.wgsl; see docs/shaders.md). `color = { r, g, b [, a] }` multiplies the picture's colours (255 leaves them; it cannot brighten). `rotation` is in radians, positive clockwise on the screen. 2D effects: `blend = "add"` (or "screen") adds light instead of covering (a glow, a spark, a muzzle flash; it can only brighten), `lit = false` keeps it out of nova.ambient2d's dark (a lit window), `foot = y` is the screen y it stands on (what puddle reflections flip it about). `flip_x = true` / `flip_y = true` mirror the picture in its own frame, before `rotation` turns it (as a negative sx or sy does).

name: nova.rect
signature: nova.rect(x, y, w, h [, color [, opts]])
doc: Draw a solid rectangle (top-left x, y) in the world layer. color is {r, g, b [, a]}. opts: `blend = "add"` (adds light: a beam, a spark) or "screen", `lit = false` (not darkened by nova.ambient2d).

name: nova.effects
signature: nova.effects("high" | "low" | "off") | nova.effects{ lights, shadows, reflections, rain, bloom = true/false }
doc: Drops 2D effects on a slow device without changing the game's own calls: "low" (no reflections or bloom, a light map an eighth of the world picture's size, half the rain), "off" (none), "high" (all, the default), or one at a time. (docs/project-format.md "2D light, shadows, reflections and rain")

name: nova.reflections
signature: nova.reflections{ strength = 0.55, ripple = 1, tint = {r, g, b} } | nova.reflections(nil)
doc: Puddles and water mirror what stands over them: the tiles a tile layer marks as reflective (`"reflect": [tile numbers]` or `true` in the scene file; tileset_make lists a city tileset's puddles and scene_write's paint copies them) show what is drawn after them, flipped about where it stands (an entity's feet when its pivot puts them at its position), darkened by `tint` and wobbling by `ripple` units. Only what lands on a reflective tile is drawn twice. It stays until changed; nil turns it off. (docs/project-format.md "2D light, shadows, reflections and rain")

name: nova.circle
signature: nova.circle(x, y, radius, color [, { soft = false, ry, blend = "add", lit }])
doc: Draw a disc centred on x, y in the world layer (screen coordinates, like nova.rect). `soft = true` fades it to nothing at its edge (a glow, a soft shadow), `ry` makes it an ellipse, `blend = "add"` adds light (a neon halo, a muzzle flash).

name: nova.light2d
signature: nova.light2d{ x, y, radius = 96, radius_y, color = {r, g, b}, intensity = 1, flicker = 0, screen = false } | nova.light2d(x, y [, opts])
doc: A 2D light for this frame (call it from a draw): brightest at x, y (world coordinates, like an entity's; screen = true for screen ones) and fading to nothing at `radius` units, an ellipse with `radius_y` (0.6 of the radius lies flat on the ground). `intensity` above 1 lights dark tiles brightly; `flicker` (0 to 1) wavers like a failing tube, the same at the same time. Seen only with nova.ambient2d. At most 128 a frame (the nearest to the middle of the view are kept; play's render line says when there were more). An entity's `light = { ... }` does this for you. (docs/project-format.md "2D light, shadows, reflections and rain")

name: nova.ambient2d
doc: Turns on 2D lighting: the world's sprites and tiles (not the HUD) are multiplied by a light map that is this colour where no light reaches, the colour a white wall shows (a night street: { 92, 100, 150 }). Lights add to it: nova.light2d, an entity's `light`. It stays until changed; nil turns lighting off. Cheap: a small light map a quarter of the world picture's size and one texture read per sprite pixel. (docs/project-format.md "2D light, shadows, reflections and rain")

name: nova.animator
signature: nova.animator(model, { start, fade, states, on_event }) -> animator
doc: A small animation state machine for a skinned or animated model. A state is `{ clip = "walk" }` (with `loop = false` to play once, `next = "idle"` for where it goes when it ends, `speed` to play faster, `fade` for its own crossfade time) or `{ blend = "speed", points = { { 0, "idle" }, { 3, "walk" }, { 7, "sprint" } } }`: the two clips nearest the number set with `anim:set("speed", v)` are mixed, their cycles kept in step. Methods: `anim:play(state [, { restart, fade }])` crossfades into a state (nothing if already in it), `anim:update(dt)` once a frame, `anim:draw(x, y, z [, options of nova.model])`, `anim:state()`, `anim:finished()` (a one-shot with nowhere to go has ended), `anim:layers()` (the `layers` for nova.model), `anim.speed` (a multiplier for all of it). Keeping time with the motion: `anim:time()` gives `clip, seconds, phase` for the state it is in (phase runs 0 to 1 over the clip; for a blend, the nearer clip), `anim:phase()` just the phase; `on_event = function(event, clip) ... end` (or `anim.on_event = ...`) is called from `update` when that clip passes one of its named events (the model file's clip "events"), and `anim:events()` lists the names passed in the last update. Use these for footsteps, not the animator's own fields.

name: nova.model
doc: Draw a 3D model. Options: scale, rx, ry, rz (radians), quat = { x, y, z, w } (a turn as a quaternion, as a physics body gives it, in place of rx, ry, rz), tint, parts (turn pieces on their own: parts = { wheel = { ry = 1 } }, see nova.model_parts; visible = false leaves a part and everything under it out of the draw: parts = { hat = { visible = false } }, and visible = true shows a part the model hides at rest (its file says "hidden": true): a face painted in several expressions of which one of each set shows), layers (clips mixed by weight; a layer with `mask = { "Spine" }` is laid over the mix on those parts and their children only; `additive = true` adds how far the clip is from the rest pose instead), clip and time (pose it from an animation clip, see nova.model_clips; loop = false holds the last pose), layers = { { clip = "walk", time = t, weight = 0.7 }, { clip = "run", time = t2, weight = 0.3 } } (several clips mixed by weight; nova.animator does the bookkeeping), shadow = false (casts no shadow, see nova.shadows), sway = 0.3 (bends in the wind: see nova.wind), rigid = true (on hills the whole model is lifted by the ground's height under its origin, not every vertex by the height under that vertex, so it is not sheared on a slope: a vehicle sets its own tilt from the ground under its wheels, see nova.terrain_height), lod = "cheaper_model" with lod_distance (100) and lod_fade (15% of the distance) metres (draws that model instead past that distance on the ground from the camera, the two trading places by a screen-door so nothing pops; also with clip, layers or parts: the far model is then a plain model in its rest pose and no pose is made), max_distance = 80 (nothing is drawn beyond that many metres on the ground from the camera, a pose is not made either), pose_step = 0.0667 (with clip: seconds; snaps time down to a multiple, so characters at the same moment of a clip share one pose and one set of GPU joint matrices; 0 = exact times only. A crowd of 300 with random phases becomes a few dozen poses), constraints = false (leaves out the rules the studio put on the model's parts: limits, copies, reach; they apply by default), morph = { smile = 0.6 } (blends the model's shape keys by name, 0 to 1 each; see nova.model_morphs; a part that bends with a skeleton ignores them), shader = "water" (draw it with shaders/water.wgsl, with params = { up to 8 numbers }, textures = { up to 2 pictures } and blend = true for see-through; see nova.post and docs/shaders.md). dirt = 0..1 puts dirt on the model with no picture: thick at its foot, its ragged edge climbing as the amount grows (further at the tail, -z), spatter above it and a thin film of dust, and no gloss, metal, clear coat or glass where it lies; dirt_color = { r, g, b } is its colour (a dull brown when left out) and dirt_on_top = true makes it lie on what faces up too (snow). Change it over time: Pine Ridge Rally's cars pick it up on gravel, sand and snow and shed it on tarmac. On the hills (nova.terrain) the renderer lifts what is drawn by the ground: every vertex by the ground under it; with `rigid = true` the model (and each piece drawn on its own, a posed part, a wheel) by the ground under that piece's own origin; with `lift = "origin"` every piece by the ground under the model's origin, as one rigid thing (a car whose wheels must not float on a slope).

name: nova.light
signature: nova.light{ dir = {x, y, z}, color = {r, g, b}, ambient = {r, g, b} }
doc: Sets the sun that lights 3D models: the direction it travels, its colour and the ambient floor. Colours are 0 to 255 multipliers (255 = full). Any field can be left out. Stays until changed.

name: nova.model_colliders
doc: The collision circles made for a model in the model editor (green rings): on the ground in the model's own frame, in metres, x across and z forward. An empty list when it has none.

name: nova.model_shapes
signature: nova.model_shapes(id) -> { circles = { { x, z, r } }, capsules = { { ax, az, bx, bz, r } }, boxes = { { x, z, hw, hl, turn } } }
doc: Everything the model editor says a model blocks, on the ground in the model's own frame, in metres: circles (the same as nova.model_colliders), capsules (a segment from a to b made r thick) and boxes (centred on x, z; hw across, hl along z; turn in radians). Scenery marked static uses all three for nova.scenery.push.

name: nova.solid
doc: Collision against the triangles of models: hills, caves, cliffs, buildings made in a 3D tool, where nova.walls' boxes and ramps are not enough. A character is a capsule that slides along walls of any angle, walks up gentle slopes (not steep ones), hops small ledges, stays on a slope going down, and bumps its head.

name: nova.solid.add
signature: nova.solid.add(model, x, y, z [, { ry, rx, rz, scale, camera_only, scene }]) -> triangles
doc: Makes a placed copy of a model's triangles solid (its whole mesh, as drawn; read from the file the first time). Draw the model yourself with nova.model at the same place. Models with thousands of triangles are fine: they are kept in a grid. `camera_only = true` makes them stop only lines of sight (`nova.solid.sightline`, the follow camera's `collide`): bodies pass through. `scene = true` has them forgotten when the scene ends. An entity with `solid = true` and a model does this for itself where it is placed, and static scenery that blocks is added `camera_only`.

name: nova.solid.move
signature: nova.solid.move(x, y, z, radius, height, dx, dy, dz [, { slope = 50, step = 0.35, snap = 0.3 }]) -> { x, y, z, ground, normal, wall, wall_normal, ceiling, stepped }
doc: Moves a capsule standing with its feet at (x, y, z), `radius` wide and `height` tall (at least twice the radius), by (dx, dy, dz), and says where it ended up. `ground` is true when it stands on something walkable (`normal` is that surface's up); `wall` when it touched a wall or a slope too steep for `slope` degrees (`wall_normal`, with a y above 0 for a steep slope: slide down it); `ceiling` when it hit its head; `stepped` is how far it hopped up a ledge of at most `step` metres. It follows ground down by up to `snap` metres so that it does not leave a slope. Give it the move for one frame (speed times dt, gravity included) and set your vertical speed to 0 when `ground` or `ceiling`; the move goes in short steps so nothing tunnels through a floor. The body also stops at static scenery that blocks (the collision circles of a tree or a post, which have no height: `nova.scenery.push`), so one call moves a walker against everything a scene has made solid; `scenery = false` in the options leaves the scenery out.

name: nova.solid.raycast
signature: nova.solid.raycast(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, max) -> distance, nx, ny, nz | nil
doc: The first solid triangle a ray hits within `max` metres: the distance to it in metres (whatever the length of the direction you give: it need not be unit length, and `max` is in metres too) and the surface's normal, facing the ray; nothing if it hits none.

name: nova.solid.sightline
signature: nova.solid.sightline(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, max) -> distance, nx, ny, nz | nil
doc: As `nova.solid.raycast`, and triangles added `camera_only` (the crowns of the scenery's trees) stop it too: what a camera's view is blocked by. `nova.cam3.follow`'s `collide` uses it.

name: nova.solid.touching
signature: nova.solid.touching(x, y, z, radius, height [, margin = 0.1]) -> model, mx, my, mz, px, py, pz | nil
doc: What stands in a body's way: the nearest solid thing that is not the ground it stands on, within `margin` metres of a capsule with its feet at x, y, z. Returns the model it was added as, where that was placed, and the point of it that is nearest; nothing when nothing is that near. For saying what blocks a walker ("against the arch").

name: nova.solid.mover
signature: nova.solid.mover() -> radius, height, step, slope | nil
doc: The body the game last moved with `nova.solid.move`: its radius and height and the step and slope it was given. The test player (`walk_to`) plans its way for that body.

name: nova.solid.clear_scene
doc: Forgets the triangles added with `scene = true` (entities with `solid = true`, the scenery's sight blockers); what the game added itself stays. The framework calls it when a scene ends.

name: nova.solid.floor_below
signature: nova.solid.floor_below(x, y, z [, max_drop = 50]) -> y, nx, ny, nz | nil
doc: The height of the first solid surface at most `max_drop` metres below a point, and its normal: where a shadow blob or an aim marker goes.

name: nova.solid.count
doc: How many solid triangles there are.

name: nova.solid.clear
doc: Forgets every solid triangle (for a change of level).

name: nova.scenery
doc: The static scenery: trees, road pieces and barriers that never move, kept cheaply and drawn only near the camera (out to `nova.scenery.range` metres if you set it, else to where the fog ends or 300 m; 0 for none; the last 12% of the range fades out instead of vanishing). An entity class with `static = true` and a model puts itself here.

name: nova.scenery.draw
doc: Draws the scenery within `radius` metres of a point. The framework already does this around the camera every frame; call it yourself only with nova.scenery.range = 0, to draw around somewhere else.

name: nova.scenery.scatter
signature: nova.scenery.scatter(model, { count, area, seed, scale, ground, min_normal_y, filter, tints, sway, max_distance, shadow, lod... }) -> placed
doc: Scatters copies of a model over an area, on the ground: grass, flowers, bushes, trees, into the static scenery (kept in Rust, drawn near the camera). `area` is { x0, z0, x1, z1 } or { x, z, radius }; `seed` makes the same field every time; `scale` is a number or { min, max }; `ground(x, z) -> height, normal_y` says where the ground is (by default the first nova.solid surface from above); spots on slopes steeper than `min_normal_y` (0.7) are refused, and so are those `filter(x, z, y, normal_y)` says no to; `tints` is a list of colours, one chosen for each. The other options are those of nova.scenery.add: `sway` (see nova.wind), `max_distance` (grass is not worth drawing far off), `shadow = false` (it casts none), `lod`. Returns how many were placed.

name: nova.scenery.add
signature: nova.scenery.add(model, x, y, z [, { ry, scale, tint, shadow, sway, max_distance, lod, lod_distance }])
doc: Puts a model into the static scenery: pieces that never move. `max_distance` stops it being drawn beyond that many metres (it fades out over the last 12%); `sway` bends it in the wind (nova.wind). `lod` names a cheaper model drawn instead beyond `lod_distance` metres (100 by default); the two trade places over `lod_fade` metres (15% of the distance by default), each fading by a screen-door, so nothing pops. It is drawn only near the camera and its collision circles block `nova.scenery.push`. A scene file's objects whose entity class has `static = true` do this for you. `shapes = false` leaves the model's collision shapes out (for a piece whose own triangles are solid).

name: nova.scenery.ahead
signature: nova.scenery.ahead(x, z, dx, dz, length [, radius]) -> distance, cx, cz, cr | nil
doc: Looks along a line from (x, z) in the direction (dx, dz) for `length` metres, as wide as a circle of `radius`, for the nearest solid circle of the static scenery. Gives how far away it is (0 if touching) and the circle's x, z and radius, or nothing. How a car or a character sees what is coming, to steer round it.

name: nova.scenery.raycast
signature: nova.scenery.raycast(x, z, dx, dz, length) -> distance, hit_x, hit_z, cx, cz, cr | nil
doc: A ray along the ground: the first solid circle of the static scenery it meets (at most `length` metres), with where it hit and the circle.

name: nova.scenery.line_clear
signature: nova.scenery.line_clear(x1, z1, x2, z2 [, radius]) -> boolean
doc: Is the straight line between two points on the ground free of solid scenery? `radius` makes the line that wide. Line of sight, or a clear path.

name: nova.scenery.push
signature: nova.scenery.push(x, z, r) -> dx, dz | nil
doc: A circle of radius r at (x, z): how far to move it to get out of the static scenery's collision circles, or nil when it is free.

name: nova.scenery.touching
signature: nova.scenery.touching(x, z, radius [, margin = 0.1]) -> model, x, z | nil
doc: The piece of static scenery a circle touches or comes within `margin` of: its model and where the piece stands. For saying what is in the way.

name: nova.scenery.clear
doc: Removes everything from the static scenery (a scene does this by itself when it ends).

name: nova.scenery.count
doc: How many pieces the static scenery holds.

name: nova.shadows
doc: Turns on the sun's shadows (set the sun with nova.light). They cover `radius` metres around what the camera looks at: a smaller radius is sharper. `strength` is how dark they are, 0 to 1. `near` (metres, 12 by default) gives the first metres in front of the camera a second, finer map, so a wheel, a foot or a post has a crisp shadow that starts where it touches the ground; 0 leaves it out (with graphics shadow_cascades 2 or 3 the cascades do this instead). `softness` (0.25 to 4, 1 by default) is how wide the soft edge is, in texels of the map. Models cast and receive them unless drawn with shadow = false (which only stops casting: such a model, the ground, still receives); see-through models never cast. Costs extra drawing, so offer a way to turn it off. `nova.shadows(nil)` turns them off.

name: nova.sky
signature: nova.sky{ top = {r, g, b}, horizon = {r, g, b} [, sun = {x, y, z}, stars = 0..1, clouds = 0..1, ground = {r, g, b}] }
doc: Paints a sky behind everything in 3D: `horizon` where it meets the ground (and below), blending up to `top` overhead. Colours are 0 to 255, as you would pick them on screen. Stays until changed; `nova.sky(nil)` goes back to the plain clear colour. `sun` is the direction towards the sun, and its height is the time of day: the sky draws a sun there (white overhead, orange as it sinks, gone under the horizon) with a halo, a glow along the horizon on the sun's side that is strongest under a low sun, clouds that it lights (bright edges towards it, dark undersides, orange at sunset), stars that come out as it sets, and a moon opposite it. The colours are yours (`top`, `horizon`: what the sky is at that hour); a game that wants a day to pass blends them with the sun's height as it moves it (Pine Ridge Rally's lib/sky.lua does, from a table of colours by the sun's height). `stars` (0 to 1) is how many stars show, `clouds` (0 to 1) how much of the sky is cloud, drifting slowly. `ground` is the colour of the land around: models lit by their materials (`"materials"` in nova.json: car paint, metal, glass) are then lit by it from below and mirror it under the horizon, and are darker near their own base, so that they take on the colours of the place they stand in.

name: nova.fog
signature: nova.fog{ color = {r, g, b}, near = 40, far = 250 }
doc: Fades 3D models into `color` between `near` and `far` metres from the camera, which hides things popping in at a distance. Use the sky's horizon colour for it to blend in. Stays until changed; `nova.fog(nil)` turns it off.

name: nova.graphics
signature: nova.graphics{ hdr, msaa, shadow_cascades, ibl, anisotropy } | nova.graphics()
doc: Opt-in quality settings of the world picture, all off by default (they can also be set in nova.json under "graphics"). `hdr = true` draws the world to a 16-bit float picture and puts it through a filmic tone curve, and bloom then works on real brightness; `msaa = 4` smooths edges with 4 samples a pixel (instead of `fxaa`); `shadow_cascades` (1 to 3) splits the sun's shadow into near and far maps with softly filtered edges; `ibl = true` lights models that use their material by the sky (`nova.sky`) and reflects it; `anisotropy` (1 to 16) keeps textures sharp on the ground at a slant. Changing a setting rebuilds the world's pipelines (a short hitch: do it from a menu), `nova.graphics()` turns everything off. Each costs GPU time; see docs/switch-class-graphics.md.

name: nova.look
signature: nova.look{ toon, outline, exposure, saturation, vignette, bloom, bloom_threshold, ao, ao_radius, blur, grade } | nova.look()
doc: How the picture is treated. `toon = 3` cuts the sun's light into that many flat bands (2 to 8; 0 is smooth); `outline = true` or `{ color = {r, g, b}, strength = 0.85, width = 1 }` draws a line where the distance to the surface jumps (the outline of things; it fades with the fog); `exposure` (1) brightens or darkens through a soft shoulder, `saturation` (1; 0 is grey), `vignette` (0 to 1) darkens the corners; `bloom` (0 to 4; 0.5 is a good start) makes what is brighter than `bloom_threshold` (0.7) glow; `ao` (0 to 1) darkens creases and the feet of things within `ao_radius` metres (0.8); `blur` (0 to 1) streaks the left and right sides of the picture as if rushing past (a speed effect for racing games: set it each frame from the speed; the middle third stays sharp). It stays until changed; `nova.look()` clears it. An outline or a colour adjustment makes the world draw through one more pass (about one extra read of the depth per pixel and four for an outline; on the Retroid bloom is about 1.3 ms and ao 0.85 ms of GPU); the toon ramp costs nothing extra. `grade = { shadows = {r, g, b}, highlights = {r, g, b} }` multiplies the darks and the lights by a colour each (255 leaves a channel alone): blue darks and warm lights for a night street. Bloom, vignette and the grade work on flat (2D) games too.

name: nova.post
doc: A full-screen post effect over the world picture (before the HUD): the custom shader shaders/<name>.wgsl, whose `shade` reads the picture with s.color and nova_scene(uv). params = { up to 8 numbers } arrive as s.param and s.param2, textures = { up to 2 pictures } as nova_texture_a/b. It stays until changed; nova.post() clears it. One extra full-screen pass at the world's resolution. See docs/shaders.md.

name: nova.shaders
doc: The project's custom shaders that compiled (`water` for shaders/water.wgsl). A shader with a mistake is listed in nova check with its line, and a draw that names it is drawn without it.

name: nova.terrain
signature: nova.terrain{ waves = { { wavelength = 400, direction = 30, height = 6, phase = 0 }, ... }, heightmap = "terrain/hills.png", x = -500, z = -500, size = 1000, height = 40 } | nova.terrain()
doc: Hills. The ground's height is the sum of up to eight sine waves over the ground: `wavelength` is metres from crest to crest, `direction` degrees on the ground (0 varies along +x, 90 along +z), `height` the metres from the middle to a crest, `phase` a shift in radians. Every model drawn near the ground (an instance whose origin is below 30 m) is lifted by the height under each of its vertices, shadows included, so a game draws on flat ground as before and the hills follow: roads, cars and trees alike. Mind the steepness: the slope of a wave is up to 2 pi x height / wavelength. `heightmap` is designed ground from a project PNG (16-bit grey is full precision; 8-bit RGB packs red as the high byte and green as the low one): `x`, `z` are the ground position of its top-left pixel, `size` the metres across (or `cell`, metres per pixel), `height` the metres white stands for; the ground between pixels is blended bilinearly, and outside the picture it keeps the edge's height. Waves given too are added on top. `nova.terrain()` makes the ground flat again.

name: nova.terrain_height
doc: The height of the ground at (x, z) under nova.terrain (0 on flat ground). Add it to a camera, a light or a particle emitter that is placed by hand; models are lifted by the renderer.

name: nova.terrain_slope
doc: How fast the ground rises there: two numbers, along x and along z (metres of height per metre). 0, 0 on flat ground.

name: nova.wind
doc: The wind that bends foliage: `direction` is degrees on the ground (0 blows towards +x, 90 towards +z), `strength` 0 to 4 (1 is a breeze). It bends models drawn with a `sway` (nova.model, nova.scenery.add, nova.scenery.scatter), more the higher a part is above the model's origin, with a slow swell that travels across the field along the wind and a quicker flutter; shadows bend with it. It stays until changed; `nova.wind()` stills it.

name: nova.point_light
signature: nova.point_light(x, y, z [, { radius = 10, color = {r, g, b}, dir = {dx, dy, dz}, angle = 50 }])
doc: A light that fades out at `radius`. Give it `dir` (the way it points) and it is a spot light: a cone `angle` degrees wide (1 to 170; 50 by default) that is full in the middle and fades to nothing at its edge, for headlights and torches (tilt it a little down so that the cone lands on the ground). Call it every frame you want it (it lasts one frame); ask for as many as you like (up to 256 a frame): the 16 nearest the camera, by the edge of their reach, are lit. When the choice changes (you walk down a row of lamps) a light fades in or out over a quarter of a second instead of switching; a light that is new is on at once and one you stop asking for is off at once (a muzzle flash is yours to time). Each lit light costs a little on every lit pixel: a game that needs fewer can use fewer.

name: nova.model_parts
doc: The names of a model's parts (nodes), for `parts = { name = { ry = 1 } }` in nova.model.

name: nova.model_pose
signature: nova.model_pose(id [, opts]) -> { [part] = { x, y, z, low }, ... }
doc: Where each part of a model is (the place of its own origin: its joint), in the model's own space (before the scale and turn you draw it with), in the pose `nova.model(id, ..., opts)` would draw: a `clip` and `time`, `layers`, and the `parts` turns. `low` is the lowest point (y) of the part's own shapes in that pose, when it has any: a foot's sole, where `y` is its ankle (the points of a bending, skinned limb count with the part that pulls them hardest; the part that only carries such a mesh has `skin = true` and no `low`). For aiming a hand, finding a foot's height, or feeding `nova.ik`.

name: nova.ik
signature: nova.ik(id, opts, { root, mid, tip }, target [, pole]) -> parts, reached
doc: Two-bone inverse kinematics: the turns that make a limb (three parts, each the child of the one before: a thigh, shin and foot; an upper arm, forearm and hand) reach `target` ({x, y, z} in the model's own space). It returns a `parts` table (a `quat` for the top two parts) to give `nova.model` with the same `opts`, and whether the target was within reach (if not, the limb stretches toward it). `pole` ({x, y, z}) is the point the middle joint bends toward (a knee toward the front); without one it bends the way it does in the pose. The bones keep their lengths. `opts` are the options you draw the model with (a clip, layers, parts); turns you give the chain's own parts there are replaced. Needs the pose, so call it every frame after choosing the clip: `local parts = nova.ik('hero', opts, { 'Thigh_L', 'Shin_L', 'Foot_L' }, target, knee); opts.parts = parts` (merge it with other turns of yours).

name: nova.model_clips
doc: The animation clips a model has, with their length in seconds, for nova.model(..., { clip = name, time = seconds }). `events` lists the clip's named moments in time order, { { t = seconds, name = "step" }, ... } (empty when it has none): they are written in the model file's clip as "events": [{ "t": 0.25, "name": "step" }] and reach code through on_clip_event and the animator's on_event.

name: nova.model_morphs
doc: The shape keys (morph targets) a model has, by name, for nova.model(..., { morph = { name = weight } }).

name: nova.camera
signature: nova.camera(ex, ey, ez, tx, ty, tz [, fov])
doc: Set the 3D camera: eye position, target position and field of view in degrees.

name: nova.clear
doc: Set the background colour (0 to 255).

name: nova.view
doc: The size of the screen in logical units, 540 high: whole numbers (rounded down), so they work with math.random and as grid sizes. nova.view("exact") gives the real width, fractional on a screen that is not 16:9: use it to put things exactly in the middle or against the right edge (nova.ui.menu does).

name: nova.time
doc: Seconds since the game started.

name: nova.log
doc: Write a line to the log.

name: nova.testing
doc: What a scripted run (the play tool, `nova run --play`) asks of the game. `nova.testing.invincible` is true in a run with "invincible": true and false otherwise: `if nova.testing.invincible then return end` at the top of a hurt function makes the hero safe in such runs when its life is not a plain `hp` or `health` field (those the run puts back itself).

name: nova.testing.drawn
signature: nova.testing.drawn(kind?, match?) -> { { kind, name, x, y, z?, w?, h? }, ... }
doc: What the frame drew (in a play run's print, after a frame: the whole frame), for tests: each draw call with its kind ("model", "sprite", "rect", "ui_sprite", "ui_rect", "ui_line", "ui_text", "ui_poly"; "ui" for all of the UI's, nil for all), its name (the picture or model, or the text's words), its place and size. `match` keeps those whose name or words contain it. Kept only in a play run (or a Rust test that called Game::record_drawn); elsewhere an error, never an empty answer. `print: ["nova.testing.drawn('ui_text')"]` lists the HUD's words.

name: nova.testing.drawn_count
doc: How many of the frame's draw calls are of that kind and contain `match` (see nova.testing.drawn): "the map is not drawn" is `nova.testing.drawn_count('ui_sprite', 'map') == 0`, with no flag in the game. An error outside a play run, so a test cannot pass by accident.

name: nova.ui
doc: Drawing in the UI layer, always at the screen's native resolution.

name: nova.image_size
doc: The size in pixels of a picture in `sprites/` (one frame of it, for a sprite sheet): for laying out panels and buttons around the art you have.

name: nova.ui.panel
signature: nova.ui.panel(id, x, y, w, h [, { slice, scale, color }])
doc: Draws a panel or button of any size from one picture without stretching its corners (a nine-slice): `slice` is how many pixels of the picture are border (a number, or { left, top, right, bottom }); the corners are drawn as they are (times `scale`), the edges stretch one way and the middle both. Ready-made panels, buttons and frames (Kenney's UI packs, for one) are nine-slices. Without `slice` a third of the picture is border. `color` tints it.

name: nova.ui.sprite
doc: Draw an image or one frame of a sprite sheet, centred on x, y, in the UI layer (screen coordinates, over the world, at the screen's own resolution). Options: scale, sx, sy, w, h, rotation (radians, positive clockwise), color = { r, g, b [, a] } (multiplies the picture's colours; 255 leaves them, a fades it), anchor, frame (of a sprite sheet), and `src = { x, y, w, h }` (draw only that part of the picture, in pixels from its top left). The same options as nova.sprite, without the custom shader.

name: nova.ui.rect
signature: nova.ui.rect(x, y, w, h [, color [, opts]])
doc: Like nova.rect, in the UI layer. Options make it a panel: `radius` (rounded corners, units), `slant` (the top edge that many units right of the bottom: a leaning banner or a wipe's slat; negative leans left), `gradient = { top_colour, bottom_colour }`, `outline = { color = {r, g, b}, width = 2 }` (inside the edge); its edges are smooth at the screen's resolution. `layer = "top"` draws it in order with the UI's text: over every text drawn before it, under every text drawn after (a dimming page over the HUD, a wipe that covers the words); without it, every UI rectangle and sprite is under all UI text.

name: nova.ui.slant
signature: nova.ui.slant(x, y, w, h, cut [, color])
doc: A panel or button with a leaning right edge: `w` wide at the top and `w - cut` at the bottom (a negative cut leans it the other way), in the UI layer. The lean is drawn a screen pixel at a time, so it is smooth at any resolution. Themes use it with `slant = cut` on a panel, a button or the focus.

name: nova.ui.line
signature: nova.ui.line(x1, y1, x2, y2, width [, color])
doc: A straight stroke `width` units thick from one point to the other, in the UI layer (one turned rectangle): for icons and arrows drawn as strokes.

name: nova.ui.text
signature: nova.ui.text(x, y, text [, opts]) -> width, height, size
doc: Draw text. Options: font, size, color, width (wrap), align, shadow, valign ("top", the default: y is the top of the line; "middle": y is the middle of the capital letters, so a label in a button looks centred; "baseline"), fallback (a font name or a list of them: if the font lacks a character of the text, the first of these that has them all draws it, instead of a box), bold (true, or a number: 1 is the usual bold; the letters are thickened, not drawn twice), outline (a colour, or { color, width } with width in logical units, default an eleventh of the size: one band round every letter, behind it). With `width`, `align` (left, center, right) places the lines inside that width; without it, "center" puts the middle of the text at x and "right" puts its right edge there. fit: "shrink" makes one line smaller until it is no wider than `width` (and no taller than `height`); "wrap" wraps it at `width` and makes it smaller until it is no taller than `height`; never below `min_size` (8); the third result is the size it was drawn at. spacing: room after every letter as a share of the size (0.2 spaces a label out like CSS letter-spacing 0.2em). line_spacing: how far apart lines are, as a multiple of the font's own (0.5 to 4; 1.5 gives the pixel fonts air). Text is always drawn over UI rectangles and sprites, whatever the order of the calls. Fonts: sans, rounded, pixel, terminal, mono, serif, comic, display, script, or a project font. `rotation` (radians, clockwise) and `zoom` turn and grow the drawn letters about x, y without drawing them again: a tilted label, a banner that slams in (`size` is what keeps letters crisp at another size). There is no skew: a slanted face is a font that leans ("comic").

name: nova.ui.text_size
doc: Measure text without drawing it (the same options as nova.ui.text, `fit` too: the third result is the size it would be drawn at).

name: nova.ui.text_width
doc: Width of text in logical units.

name: nova.input
doc: Named input actions. Projects bind actions to keys, buttons, sticks and touch in nova.json.

name: nova.input.down
doc: True while the action is held.

name: nova.input.pressed
doc: True in the one game step after the action went down.

name: nova.input.released
doc: True in the one game step after the action was let go.

name: nova.input.axis
doc: -1 to 1 for axes such as move_x; 0 to 1 for buttons.

name: nova.input.actions
doc: Every action name.

name: nova.input.bind
doc: Change what drives an action. A list of sources makes a button; { negative = {...}, positive = {...} } makes an axis.

name: nova.input.bindings
doc: The sources an action uses.

name: nova.input.reset_bindings
doc: Restore the project's own bindings.

name: nova.input.next_source
doc: The source pressed since you last asked (each press is reported once), such as "key:KeyZ" or "pad:south", or nil. For "press the new key" screens: call it once when you start listening, to drop the press that opened the screen, then every frame.

name: nova.input.pointer
signature: nova.input.pointer() -> { present, x, y, dx, dy, down, right, middle, pressed, released, wheel }
doc: The mouse, or the first finger when there is no mouse, as this step sees it: where it is in the game's own units (as nova.view() measures them), how far it moved since the last step, which buttons are down, whether the main button went down (`pressed`) or up (`released`) since the last step (each once, even on a fast screen), and the wheel. With the mouse locked, dx and dy are how far it was pushed.

name: nova.input.grab_mouse
doc: Locks the cursor to the window and hides it, so that the mouse can turn a camera without end (nova.input.pointer().dx and dy are then the pushes); false frees it. Where the platform cannot, nothing happens.

name: nova.input.rumble
signature: nova.input.rumble(strength, seconds [, player]) or nova.input.rumble{ strong, weak, seconds, player }
doc: Shakes a player's controller for a moment: strength from 0 to 1 (strong is the big motor, weak the small one), up to 5 seconds. Without a player every pad shakes. On Android a controller with a motor shakes, and the handheld itself shakes for its built-in controls; a player on another device (local co-op) feels it too. Pads that cannot rumble ignore it, so it is always safe to call.

name: nova.input.players
signature: nova.input.players() -> { { player, name, connected, remote, rumble }, ... }
doc: The players seated now: each pad keeps its player number while connected and gets it back when it reconnects; player 1 is always this device (keyboard too). Players on another device (local co-op) are listed with remote = true.

name: nova.input.player_events
doc: What happened to the players since the last call: kind is "joined", "left" (its seat is kept) or "back".

name: nova.input.player
signature: nova.input.player(n) -> { down, pressed, released, axis, prompt, bindings, bind, rumble, number }
doc: The input calls for one player: local p = nova.input.player(2); if p.pressed("jump") then ... end.

name: nova.input.glyph
doc: What a button says on a Nintendo-style pad (pad:south is "B", pad:east "A") and an icon name ("button_b"; Kenney's Switch prompts are "switch_" .. icon). Keys are named as on the keyboard.

name: nova.input.prompt
signature: nova.input.prompt(action [, player [, keys]]) -> label, icon, source
doc: The button to show for an action (its first gamepad source, or with keys = true its first key), as nova.input.glyph names it.

name: nova.input.save_controls
doc: Keeps the bindings the player chose (nova.input.bind, for everyone or one player) for the next run; they are read back when the game starts.

name: nova.net
doc: Local co-op over wifi: one device hosts, others on the same network find it and join (needs "local_network": true in nova.json).

name: nova.net.host
doc: Starts hosting: other devices on this wifi can find the game and join, up to `players` (2 to 4) in all. The host runs the game; joined players are more players (nova.input.down("jump", 2)).

name: nova.net.find
signature: nova.net.find() -> { { id, name, players, max, full }, ... }
doc: The games of this kind on this wifi; keeps looking while it is called (every frame on a "Join" screen).

name: nova.net.join
doc: Joins a game from nova.net.find() (or an address typed by hand, such as "192.168.1.20"). Watch nova.net.status() for "joined" or "lost".

name: nova.net.leave
doc: Stops hosting, looking or playing (the others are told).

name: nova.net.status
doc: "off", "hosting", "finding", "joining", "joined" or "lost", and a sentence to show ("Waiting for players", "Lost the connection to Jasper's Retroid").

name: nova.net.is_host
doc: True while this device hosts the game.

name: nova.net.me
doc: This device's player number in the game (1 on the host and when not connected).

name: nova.net.name
doc: What this device is called to the others (its name as the owner set it, or the name given to host/join).

name: nova.net.address
doc: This device's address on the local network, to type into another device by hand.

name: nova.net.players
signature: nova.net.players() -> { { player, name, me, host, ping }, ... }
doc: Everyone in the game; ping is the time there and back in milliseconds.

name: nova.net.events
doc: Since the last call: "joined" and "left" players, "connected" (this device joined) and "lost" (the host went away).

name: nova.net.send
doc: A message that arrives, in order: the host sends to one player or everyone; a joined device sends to the host. Numbers, strings, booleans and tables of those; under 32 KB.

name: nova.net.receive
doc: The messages that arrived since the last call.

name: nova.net.state
signature: nova.net.state(t) on the host; nova.net.state() -> t, age on a joined device
doc: The host sets what the joined devices draw, sent every frame (newest wins); a joined device reads the newest and how many seconds old it is. Use lists, not tables keyed by player numbers.

name: nova.input.last_source
doc: The most recently pressed input source, such as key:KeyZ (for rebinding screens).

name: nova.sound
doc: Sound effects (WAV files).

name: nova.sound.play
doc: Play a sound effect (or a random sound group: the name of a sounds/<name>.group.json). Options: volume, pan, pitch, loop, `vary` (0 to 0.5: each play a little higher or lower and quieter, so a repeated sound is not a row of copies; 0.05 is a little), `reverb` (0 to 1: how much of it goes to the room set with `nova.sound.room`), and limit (at most that many copies of this sound at once: one more makes the oldest copy give way, so a flood of hits cannot steal a voice from other sounds; there are 32 voices in all). `at = {x, y, z}` puts the sound at a place in the world: it is quieter the further the camera is from it (to nothing at `range` metres, 32 by default; `falloff` is "smooth" (the default, a square law), "linear", "natural" (loud close up, then a long fade) or "none" (full volume right to the range)) and comes from the left or right of where the camera looks; beyond its range a one-shot sound is not played at all (it returns 0).

name: nova.sound.group
doc: The random sound group of that name (sounds/<name>.group.json), or nil. A group is played like any sound: nova.sound.play("footsteps") picks one of its sounds each time, with volume, pitch and pan varied inside the ranges the file gives ({ "sounds": ["step1", "step2"], "volume": [0.8, 1], "pitch": [0.95, 1.05], "pan": [-0.1, 0.1], "no_repeat": true }).

name: nova.sound.stop
doc: Stop one sound, optionally fading out over fade seconds.

name: nova.sound.set
signature: nova.sound.set(id, { volume, pan, pitch, reverb, at, range })
doc: Change a sound that is playing: its volume, pan, pitch or reverb send (any of them). The change glides over a few milliseconds, so call it every frame to make a looping engine follow the revs. A sound that has ended ignores it. `at = {x, y, z}` (and `range`) makes it follow a place in the world as `play` does: call it every frame for a sound that moves or a camera that does.

name: nova.sound.room
doc: Sets the reverb that sounds go to when they are played (or set) with `reverb = 0.3` (0 to 1, how much of the sound is sent): `size` (0 to 1) is how long it rings, `damping` (0 to 1) how dull the tail is, `mix` (0 to 2) how loud the reverb is. One room is shared by all sounds; `nova.sound.room()` takes it away. It is a Freeverb-style room (eight comb filters and four all-passes a side), and costs a little CPU on the audio thread while it is on. Music (streamed Ogg) can be sent to it too with `nova.music.play(name, { reverb = ... })`.

name: nova.sound.stop_all
doc: Stop every sound effect.

name: nova.sound.volume
doc: Master volume for effects (0 to 2).

name: nova.engine_sound
doc: A car's engine and the sounds of driving, played from the loops engine_make and driving_sounds_make write: the two engine bands either side of the revs crossfaded at the engine's note, throttle-down and lifted layers by how hard it pulls, the limiter, gear changes, a turbo's breath and blow-off, pops, tyres by surface, the squeal, wind, bumps and scrapes; rivals placed where their cars are. Opt in with require; engine_sound.SURFACES (the tyre loops by surface) may be changed.

name: nova.engine_sound.new
doc: (After local engine_sound = require("nova.engine_sound"): engine_sound.new.) An engine from its profile (the table engine_make writes to engines/<name>.lua: sound, idle, max, cycles, rise, fall, gain, limiter, shift, turbo...). Then every step engine:update(dt, { rpm or rev (0 to 1), throttle (0 to 1), speed (m/s), slip, surface (road, gravel, dirt, snow, sand, rough), lift, scrape, x, y, z }); engine:shift("up" or "down") at a gear change; engine:state() -> heard rpm, load; engine:silence() (paused); engine:stop(). A rival (rival = true) plays only its throttle-down loops, placed at its x, y, z.

name: nova.engine_sound.cars
doc: Every car's engine for this step: each car table has `engine` and what engine:update takes, plus x, z, velx, velz; `player` is the driven one. Rivals within 90 m are heard from where they are, their note bent by their closing speed, with a whoosh as one passes close; `car.shifted` ("up" or "down") is played and cleared.

name: nova.music
doc: Background music: one track at a time.

name: nova.music.play
doc: Play music. Loops by default. Options: volume, fade, loop, restart. Playing the song that is already playing carries on where it is (a door between two rooms with one song does not restart it; a given `volume` is applied) and returns the same id; `restart = true` starts it again from the top.

name: nova.music.stop
doc: Stop the music. `fade_seconds` is a number, not a table: nova.music.stop(0.5) fades out over half a second.

name: nova.music.volume
doc: Master volume for music (0 to 2).

name: nova.music.position
doc: How far into the current music track it is, in seconds (nil when no music plays). For a looping track it wraps once the track has played through. It updates every frame, a little behind what you hear.

name: nova.music.layers
signature: nova.music.layers({ names }, { levels, bpm, beats, bar, volume, fade })
doc: Adaptive music: play the stems of one piece (the files the studio's Stems export writes) together and in step, each at its own level from 0 to 1 (levels = {1, 0, 0}). Give bpm and beats (or bar, in seconds) so level changes can wait for a bar line. Replaces any music that plays; it cannot be seeked. Silent stems keep playing so they stay in step.

name: nova.music.layer
doc: Fade one stem of the layered music to a level from 0 to 1 over fade seconds. at = "bar" waits for the music's next bar line (needs bpm or bar in nova.music.layers); the default is now.

name: nova.music.seek
doc: Jump the current music to a time in the track. Returns false when no music is playing. A streamed (Ogg) track finds the spot quickly, so even far jumps are heard within a few tens of milliseconds.

name: nova.save
doc: Values kept between runs of the game.

name: nova.save.get
doc: Read a saved value.

name: nova.save.set
doc: Save a number, string, boolean or table of those.

name: nova.save.delete
doc: Forget a saved value.

name: nova.save.keys
doc: Every saved key, sorted.

name: nova.save.flush
doc: Write the save file now (it is also written every few seconds and on exit).

name: nova.start
doc: Hand the frame to the framework and begin with this scene (scenes/<name>.lua).

name: nova.on_update
doc: A game-wide hook that outlives every scene: fn(dt) runs once a frame (real seconds: not slowed by nova.time_scale, not stopped by nova.pause), after the scene's own work. For a wipe that crosses a scene change, a clock, music that follows the game. Returns a function that takes the hook away. Call it from main.lua; goto_scene does not clear it.

name: nova.on_draw_ui
doc: A game-wide hook that outlives every scene: fn() runs after the scene's draw_ui, so what it draws is over all of the scene's UI (a wipe, a fade, a persistent overlay; with nova.ui.rect's `layer = "top"` it covers the scene's text too). Returns a function that takes the hook away.

name: nova.entity
doc: Define an entity class. Spec: sprite, model, tags, depth, hitbox, screen, settings, and default fields. settings = { speed = { 4, min = 0, max = 10, help = "..." }, paint = { "#ff8800", type = "colour" }, mood = { "calm", choices = { "calm", "angry" } } } declares what a scene may set: a default, a type (number, boolean, text, choice, colour, vector, object, sprite, sound, music, model), limits, a step and help; values are checked and colours arrive as { r, g, b }. The engine's own fields, which your code must not use for anything else: x, y, z; vx, vy, vz (the engine adds them to the position every step: keep your own speed there only if you do not also move the entity yourself, or say `velocity = false` in the spec and they are yours); sx, sy, angle, alpha, visible, tint, depth, frame, flip_x, flip_y, id, name; for a model rx, ry, rz, quat, parts, clip, clip_time, clip_loop, clip_speed; shader, shader_params, shader_textures, blend; and everything that starts with an underscore. `tint = { r, g, b }` MULTIPLIES the picture's colours (255, 255, 255 leaves them): it darkens or colours and can never make a sprite brighter or white, so for a hit flash blink `alpha` or `visible`, or show a white copy of the frame (sprite_write's { copy = n, silhouette = true }). `angle` is in radians and a positive angle turns the picture clockwise on the screen (y points down): 0 is as drawn, math.pi / 2 a quarter turn clockwise; the same goes for angle_to and set_velocity, where 0 is to the right and math.pi / 2 is down. A solid thing (one a mover stops at) is never overlapped, so its on_collide_<tag> never runs: notice it with self:near(tag, margin). `solid = true` with a `model` makes the model's triangles solid where the entity is placed (`nova.solid`): bodies moved with `nova.solid.move` stop at it and climb it, and the follow camera's `collide` keeps it out of the view. It is for things that stay where they are; the triangles are forgotten when the scene ends. A scene object may say it too (`"props": { "solid": true }`). 2D effects (each off until asked for): `shadow = true` (a soft ellipse under the feet, as wide as the hitbox; or { w, h, alpha, y }), `light = { radius, radius_y, color, intensity, flicker, x, y }` (a 2D light that goes with the entity, seen with nova.ambient2d; x, y move it from the entity), `blend = "add"` (its sprite adds light; a model's `blend` is a true/false of its own), `lit = false` (its sprite is not darkened by nova.ambient2d). Game time: `time_scale = 0.5` runs this entity at half speed, `unscaled = true` keeps it in real time whatever nova.time_scale and nova.hit_stop do. `hitbox_units = "world"` measures the hitbox in world units, so sx and sy (the drawing's scale) leave it alone; a negative sx still mirrors it.

name: nova.scene
doc: Define a scene class with enter, update, draw, draw_ui and leave methods.

name: nova.scene_data
doc: A scene file's data (scenes/<name>.scene.json, checked as when the scene is built: objects, images, texts, tilemaps, camera...) without going to that scene, or nil when the file does not exist. For levels kept as scene files and played by one scene: nova.scene_data("levels.3") reads scenes/levels/3.scene.json.

name: nova.t
doc: The text for a key in the chosen language (locales/<code>.json), else in the default language (en, or the first file), else the key itself. {name} in the text is replaced from vars; with vars.count the key can have .one and .other forms.

name: nova.locale
doc: Languages: one locales/<code>.json file per language, edited in the studio's Languages table.

name: nova.locale.set
doc: Choose the language, for example "fr". An error when there is no locales/<code>.json.

name: nova.locale.get
doc: The language in use (the default one until set).

name: nova.locale.available
doc: The language codes the project has files for, sorted.

name: nova.goto_scene
doc: Replace the scene at the start of the next frame; extra arguments go to enter().

name: nova.restart_scene
doc: Rebuild the current scene from its file.

name: nova.current_scene
doc: The name of the running scene. It is already the new scene's name inside an entity's create() and the scene's enter() while that scene is being built, so an entity can key what it remembers by scene.

name: nova.scene_now
doc: The scene that is running, the object itself (what `self` is in the scene's own functions), so an entity can reach its scene: `nova.scene_now().score = nova.scene_now().score + 1`, or `nova.scene_now():gem_taken(self)`. Nil before the first scene starts. nova.current_scene() is its name.

name: nova.named
doc: The living entity that the running scene file names so (an object's "name"): for a setting of type "object", nova.named(self.follow). Ask in update; names are set once the whole scene is built.

name: nova.spawn
doc: Create an entity from entities/<kind>.lua.

name: nova.particles
doc: A particle emitter. spec: rate (per second), life, speed, size, size_end, color, color_end, gravity, drag, angle, spread, spin, area, image, max, screen, depth. Ranges are {min, max}. In 3D (spec.model = a model name, with a z) y is up and spec.dir / spread aim a cone. Soft sprites: spec.sprite = a PNG in sprites/fx/ (frame = n | "random", animate = true for a sheet) draws camera-facing blended quads instead of models. Ground: ground = true (floor at ground_y, 0), or a function(x, z) -> height; bounce, ground_drag, land = "die", ground_radius. Call emitter:burst(n) for a puff, emitter:stop() to stop and let the rest fade. In 2D, `blend = "add"` makes the particles add light (sparks, embers) and `shape = "soft"` (a glow that fades to its edge) or "disc" draws round ones.

name: nova.burst
doc: One puff of spec.count (default 12) particles that removes itself afterwards. Same spec as nova.particles.

name: nova.each
doc: Call fn for every living entity with the tag (a tag from `tags = { ... }`, not a file name).

name: nova.all
doc: A new list of the living entities with the tag (a tag from `tags = { ... }`, not a file name).

name: nova.first
doc: The first living entity with the tag (nil when there is none). It takes a TAG (one of an entity's `tags = { ... }`), not the name of its file: nova.first("slime") finds nothing if slimes are tagged "enemy" (the log says so once). For one particular thing use the name the scene file gave it: nova.named("hero").

name: nova.count
doc: How many living entities have the tag (a tag from `tags = { ... }`, not a file name).

name: nova.stats
signature: nova.stats() -> { fps, lua_ms, render_ms, draws, triangles, sprites, memory_kb, entities, scenery, physics_ms, bodies }
doc: How the last frame went, for an on-screen profiler: frames a second, what your scripts took and what drawing took (milliseconds), draw calls, triangles and sprites drawn, the scripts' memory (KB), live entities and static scenery pieces, and the last physics step (milliseconds, within the scripts' time) and how many bodies there are.

name: nova.raycast
signature: nova.raycast(x, y, dx, dy, length, tag [, { ignore, height, slope }]) -> entity, distance, hit_x, hit_y | nil
doc: A ray against the entities with `tag` that have a hitbox (circles and boxes); the ground plane is x, y in a flat game and x, z after nova.collision{ plane = "xz" }. Gives the nearest hit, how far along, and where. `ignore` skips an entity (the shooter). In a ground-plane game `height` is where the ray starts and `slope` how much it rises per metre, so a shot passes over a thing whose hitbox has a `height` (and a `base`) that it does not reach.

name: nova.cam3
doc: A ready-made 3D camera: cam3.follow, cam3.first_person, cam3.look, cam3.ray and cam3.ground_point. cam3.yaw and cam3.pitch (radians) say where it looks; yaw 0 looks towards -z, positive turns left.

name: nova.cam3.eye
doc: Where the camera is, as { x, y, z } (set by follow and first_person).

name: nova.cam3.target
doc: What the camera looks at, as { x, y, z } (set by follow and first_person).

name: nova.cam3.follow
signature: nova.cam3.follow(target [, { distance, height, look_height, smooth, fov, dt, collide, margin, min_distance, hide, behind }])
doc: A camera behind and above `target` (an entity or { x, y, z }), looking at it and easing after it as it moves. distance 9, height 8, look_height 1, smooth 6 (0 stays rigidly behind), fov 60. Turn it with cam3.yaw or cam3.look. `collide = true` keeps solid things from coming between the camera and what it looks at: when a triangle added with nova.solid.add, an entity with `solid = true`, or a piece of static scenery that blocks (a tree: its whole shape, crown and all) (a wall, a hill, the level's mesh) is on the line of sight, the camera moves in along that line to `margin` (0.3) in front of it, never nearer than 0.5, and eases back out when the way is clear. It costs one nova.solid.raycast a frame. The camera eases in from where it was: pass smooth = 0 for the first frames of a scene to start behind the target. Squeezed (under an arch, against a wall) the camera comes in as near as 0.5, and the picture is the back of a head: `min_distance = 1.7` says how near is too near, and `hide = true` then stops drawing the target (its `visible`) for as long as the camera is nearer than that, so the player sees the scene instead; it is drawn again when the camera is back out. `nova.cam3.distance` is how far the camera is from what it looks at and `nova.cam3.squeezed` whether that is under `min_distance`, for a game that would rather fade the target itself (a model drawn with its own alpha) or lift the camera. `behind = 1.2` swings the camera round behind the way the target moves, that many radians a second at most (not while it walks straight at the camera); skip it on frames the player turns the camera.

name: nova.cam3.first_person
doc: A camera at `target`'s head (height 1.6, fov 75) looking where cam3.yaw and cam3.pitch say.

name: nova.cam3.look
doc: Turns the camera by some radians (a look stick, a mouse moved); pitch stops short of straight up and down.

name: nova.cam3.forward
doc: The ground direction the camera looks along: what "forward" on a stick should mean.

name: nova.cam3.right
doc: The ground direction to the camera's right.

name: nova.cam3.ray
signature: nova.cam3.ray(x, y) -> ox, oy, oz, dx, dy, dz
doc: The ray from the camera through a point of the screen (in the units nova.view() measures). The middle of the screen is straight ahead.

name: nova.cam3.ground_point
signature: nova.cam3.ground_point(x, y [, height]) -> x, z | nil
doc: Where the ray through a screen point meets the flat plane at `height` (default 0), or nothing when it looks away from it: aiming at the ground under a mouse or a finger.

name: nova.collision
doc: Tells the engine what "the ground" is for collisions, distances and neighbour queries: plane "xy" (a flat game, the default) or "xz" (a 3D game, where y is height); in "xz", `on_collide_<tag>`, `distance_to`, `angle_to`, `move_toward`, `nova.nearest` and `nova.in_radius` use x and z, and a hitbox { r = 1 } is a circle on the ground. `cell` is the size of the squares the broad phase sorts entities into, about the size of the things that collide (metres in 3D). Call it once, early.

name: nova.nearest
doc: The closest entity with the tag.

name: nova.in_radius
signature: nova.in_radius(x, y, radius, tag [, list]) -> list
doc: Entities with the tag within a distance of a point.

name: nova.send
doc: Call a method on one entity, or on every entity with a tag.

name: nova.play_anim
signature: nova.play_anim(name [, { target, targets, speed, loop, from, on_finish, pausable }]) -> player
doc: Play the keyframe animation `animations/<name>.anim.json` (made in the studio's timeline editor). `target` is what the file's "self" means (the scene when left out); `targets` names other things. Returns a player: `:pause()`, `:resume()`, `:stop()`, `:seek(seconds)`, `:playing()`, `:finished()`, `:length()`, and the fields `time` and `speed` (below 0 plays backwards). `on_finish(target, player)` runs when a one-shot animation reaches its end. Playing the same animation on the same target again replaces it. Animations on an entity hold while `nova.pause` is on; on the scene they keep going.

name: nova.stop_anims
doc: Stop every animation playing on `target`, or every animation when none is given.

name: nova.anim_data
doc: The checked contents of `animations/<name>.anim.json`, with every default filled in, without playing it.

name: nova.anims_playing
doc: How many keyframe animations are playing.

name: nova.update_anims
doc: Advance the keyframe animations by `dt` seconds. Only for a game that does not use `nova.start` (the framework does this every step).

name: nova.hitch
doc: Writes a line to the log for every frame that took longer than `ms` milliseconds (0 turns it off): the frame's time, the scene, the GPU's time, the draw calls and the script's time, then whatever `describe()` returns (a string: the car's speed, what was on screen). It is how a stutter found on a device is traced from its log (adb logcat).

name: nova.weather
signature: nova.weather{ rain = 0.5, wind = 0.3, color = {r, g, b, a} } (2D) | nova.weather{ kind = "snow", count = 300, radius = 22, height = 16, fall = 2.2, drift = 1, size = 0.07, sprite = "fx/flake", color = {r, g, b, a} } (3D) | nova.weather()
doc: In a flat game, `rain = 0 to 1`: slanted streaks over the world and splash rings on the ground (brighter rings on reflective puddles), drawn under the HUD by the renderer from nothing but their number (no Lua per drop); `wind` slants them (sideways units per unit of fall, 0.25), `color` with an alpha (170, 190, 230, 120). In 3D: fills the air around the camera with snow (soft round flakes that face you, or a `sprite` from sprites/fx/) or rain (streaks: kind = \"rain\"). The flakes are a fixed pattern that wraps round the camera as it moves and falls with nova.time(), so nothing is spawned or kept, and they stop while the game is paused. `nova.weather()` clears it. (docs/project-format.md "2D light, shadows, reflections and rain")

name: nova.scenery.push_capsule
signature: nova.scenery.push_capsule(ax, az, bx, bz, r) -> dx, dz | nil
doc: A capsule (the segment from (ax, az) to (bx, bz) thickened by `r`: a car's length, a long barrier) against the scenery's collision circles: the push that gets it out of whatever it overlaps, or nil. `nova.scenery.push` is the same for one circle.

name: nova.pause
doc: Freeze entities (the scene and timers keep running), for pause menus. The engine's own clock stops too (nova.time, the wind, the clouds and stars) and carries on from the same moment when you call nova.pause(false).

name: nova.quit
doc: End the game cleanly after this frame: the save is written, the sound stops, the window and the GPU surface are dropped, and the program exits with status 0 (for a Quit entry in a desktop or handheld menu). Closing the window and the system's own requests (SIGTERM from a handheld's "Exit game", Ctrl-C, SIGHUP) end it the same way, within a second. On Android it does nothing (an app does not end itself there: the player leaves with Home or Back) and says so in the log.

name: nova.time_scale
doc: How fast the game's time runs: 1 is normal, 0.5 slow motion, 0 stopped (0 to 100). With a tag only the entities with that tag are slowed or sped up (nova.time_scale(0.4, "enemy"): the enemies' time crawls while the hero's runs on); scales multiply. Every entity's update, sprite and model animation, velocity and timers (self:after, every, go, tween) get the scaled dt, as do keyframe animations and the scene's update; an entity whose dt is 0 is not updated at all, and nothing collides while the whole game's time stands still. An entity with `unscaled = true` (a pause menu, the HUD, a hero that is never slowed) always runs in real time, and one with `time_scale = 0.5` runs at half of whatever it would; a scene with `unscaled = true` gets real time too. Given nothing, it says the scale. The scales stay across scenes until changed; nova.time() is real time.

name: nova.hit_stop
doc: Hold the game's time still for this long (3 / 60 is three frames): the freeze frame of a heavy hit. Everything that nova.time_scale slows stops (unscaled things run on: the camera's shake, a pause menu), from the next step; a longer hit-stop while one is going lengthens it, a shorter one is left out. A scene change ends it. Given nothing, it says how long is left.

name: nova.count_alive
doc: How many entities are alive.

name: nova.wait
doc: Inside self:go(): pause the script.

name: nova.wait_until
doc: Inside self:go(): wait until fn() is true.

name: nova.ease
doc: Easing functions for tweens and keyframes: linear, in_quad, out_quad, in_out_quad, in_cubic, out_cubic, in_out_cubic, in_sine, out_sine, in_out_sine, in_back, out_back, in_out_back, out_bounce, out_elastic.

name: nova.cam
doc: The 2D camera.

name: nova.cam.set
doc: Put the camera's centre at a world point. This also stops nova.cam.follow: the camera stays where you put it until you call follow again.

name: nova.cam.follow
doc: Follow an entity; lerp 1 locks on, smaller values trail behind (0.1 is smooth). The camera starts on the entity if it was not placed yet in this scene; snap = true jumps to it now (after a door, a respawn). A scene smaller than the screen is centred by its width and height limit.

name: nova.cam.to_screen
doc: Where a world point is on the screen. An entity's own sprite is placed for you; when you draw in the world yourself (nova.sprite, nova.rect in a draw method) convert first: nova.sprite("sword", nova.cam.to_screen(self.x + 8, self.y)).

name: nova.cam.to_world
doc: The world point under a screen point (the pointer, say): the opposite of nova.cam.to_screen.

name: nova.cam.limit
doc: Keep the view inside a world rectangle.

name: nova.cam.shake
doc: Jolt the 2D camera by up to `amount` world units for `seconds` (0.2), fading out: the screen shake of a heavy hit. Only the picture moves (nova.cam.position, following and to_world are left alone); it runs in real time, through a hit-stop. A weaker shake while a stronger one is going is left out; nova.cam.shake(0) stops it. The pattern is the same every run.

name: nova.cam.position
doc: The camera centre.

name: nova.tilemap
doc: Create a tile grid. Spec: image, tile_width, tile_height, tiles, solid, x, y, depth, scale (how big a tile is drawn for each of its pixels: 0.5 for a tileset painted at twice its shown size).

name: nova.solid_at
doc: True when a world point is inside a solid tile.

name: nova.Entity
doc: The base entity class (call nova.Entity.draw(self) from a custom draw).

name: nova.Picture
doc: The built-in picture entity used by scene files.

name: nova.Text
doc: The built-in text entity used by scene files.

name: destroy
doc: Remove the entity.

name: is_alive
doc: False once destroyed.

name: distance_to
doc: Distance to a point or entity.

name: angle_to
doc: Angle to a point or entity, in radians: 0 is to the right, math.pi / 2 is down the screen (y points down), so it grows clockwise. It is the angle to give `self.angle` to point a sprite drawn facing right at the target.

name: move_toward
doc: Step toward a point; true on arrival.

name: set_velocity
doc: Set vx and vy from an angle (radians: 0 is to the right, math.pi / 2 is down the screen, so positive turns clockwise) and a speed. The engine then moves the entity by them every step.

name: speed
doc: Current speed.

name: overlaps
doc: Whether two entities' hitboxes overlap.

name: touching
doc: The first overlapping entity with the tag (nil when none). The usual way to stop at solid things: move, and if self:touching("solid") take the move back. Because of that a solid thing is never overlapped by what it stops: use self:near(tag) to notice it.

name: near
doc: The first living entity with the tag whose hitbox is within `margin` units of this one's (touching or not), or nil. For things a mover stops at, which never overlap and so never get on_collide_<tag>: a chest opens with `if self:near("hero", 6) and nova.input.pressed("a") then ... end`, a sign shows its text while `self:near("hero", 8)`. Hitboxes are compared as boxes.

name: bounds
doc: The entity's hitbox in the world.

name: slide
signature: self:slide(dx, dy [, { solid = tag }]) -> blocked_x, blocked_y, thing
doc: Move, stopping against solid tiles (and with `solid = "tag"` against the hitboxes of the entities with that tag; `thing` is the one it ran into). One that starts inside something solid is moved out the nearest way by no more than its own size; deeper in (x, y set into a wall), back to where a slide last found it free, or for one made there the nearest free place: never thrown through a wall nor left stuck in one.

name: play
doc: Play an animation tag of the entity's sprite sheet (sprites/<name>.sprite.json). Calling it again with the same tag keeps going, so it can be called every frame; the one option is `restart = true`, which starts the tag over. on_animation_end(tag) runs when a tag that does not loop finishes. `speed` sets how fast clips play (the entity's `anim_speed`, 1 as drawn, 2 twice as fast), and stays until changed: give it on every call to keep a run's feet in step (speed = v / the speed the run was drawn for).

name: play_clip
doc: Play an animation clip of the entity's 3D model. on_clip_end(name) runs when a non-looping clip finishes; on_clip_event(event, clip) runs each time the clip passes one of its named events (the model file's clip "events": a foot landing, so `function Hero:on_clip_event(event) if event == "step" then nova.sound.play("step") end end` keeps footsteps in time, also when the clip loops); set self.clip_speed to scale time.

name: clip_events
doc: The named events of the clip the entity is playing, in time order (empty when it has none or nothing plays). The entity's on_clip_event(event, clip) is called as the clip passes each.

name: stop_clip
doc: Stop the entity's model animation clip (the model returns to its authored pose).

name: stop_animation
doc: Stop animating.

name: frame_hitbox
signature: self:frame_hitbox() -> { x, y, w, h } or nil
doc: The hitbox the sprite sheet gives the frame being shown ("hitbox" and "frame_data" in its .sprite.json), in pixels from the frame's top left; nil when the sheet gives none.

name: frame_pivot
doc: The pivot (where the sprite stands) the sheet gives the frame being shown, in pixels from the frame's top left; nil when it gives none. Define on_animation_event(name, frame) to hear the events a sheet puts on frames.

name: set_frame
doc: Show one frame of the sprite sheet.

name: after
doc: Run fn once later; cancelled if the entity is destroyed.

name: every
doc: Run fn repeatedly.

name: go
doc: Run a script that can nova.wait().

name: tween
doc: Glide fields to new values.

name: play_anim
doc: Play a keyframe animation with this entity (or scene) as its "self": the same as `nova.play_anim(name, { target = self, ... })`.

name: draw
doc: Draw the entity (override for custom drawing).

name: nova.noise2
signature: nova.noise2(x, z [, seed, octaves, gain]) -> number
doc: Smooth, repeatable noise from about -1 to 1 for a place on the ground: the same answer every time for the same seed. `octaves` adds finer layers (each twice as fine, `gain` as strong; 0.5 by default).

name: nova.noise3
signature: nova.noise3(x, y, z [, seed, octaves, gain]) -> number
doc: The same noise in three dimensions: for caves, clouds and anything that changes with height.

name: nova.hash
doc: A repeatable random number from 0 up to 1 for a place (whole numbers: the block it is in). Use it instead of math.random when the same place must always give the same answer, like where a tree stands.

name: nova.voxel
doc: A world of blocks, like a block-building game: chunks of 16 x 128 x 16 blocks, lit by the sun and torches, drawn with soft shading, with a ray and a walking box for gameplay. Block (x, y, z) fills x to x+1, y to y+1, z to z+1; y is up. Call `atlas` and `block` once at load, make chunks, then call `draw` every frame after setting the camera.

name: nova.voxel.atlas
doc: The picture all blocks take their faces from: a square PNG of equal square tiles, counted from the top left along each row (tile 0, 1, 2 ...). Call it before any `block`.

name: nova.voxel.block
doc: Defines a kind of block and gives its number (1, 2, 3 ... in order; air is 0). Options: tile (all faces) or top, bottom, side, or tiles = {+x, -x, top, bottom, +z, -z}; solid (a body cannot enter), opaque (hides what is behind and stops light), liquid, shape = "cube" | "cross" (flowers, grass) | "torch", glow (0-15 light it gives), dim (light it swallows: water, leaves), cull_same (no faces between two of them: glass), alpha (0-255, less is see-through).

name: nova.voxel.id
doc: The number of a block by name.

name: nova.voxel.info
signature: nova.voxel.info(block) -> { name, solid, opaque, liquid, glow, shape, tile, side_tile }
doc: What a block is. A block is its number or its name everywhere.

name: nova.voxel.get
doc: The block at a place (air outside the height of the world and in chunks that are not loaded). Positions can be fractions: the block they fall in.

name: nova.voxel.set
doc: Puts a block in without lighting or drawing it: for building a chunk before `finish_chunk`. Use `edit` for changes during play.

name: nova.voxel.edit
doc: Changes a block during play: updates the light, the picture, and what is remembered for saving. False when the chunk is not loaded.

name: nova.voxel.fill
signature: nova.voxel.fill(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, block) -> count
doc: Fills a box (corners included) the way `set` does, quickly.

name: nova.voxel.carve
signature: nova.voxel.carve(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, { through, seed, scale, threshold, kind, squash }) -> count
doc: Digs caves into a box wherever 3D noise says so, but only out of the blocks listed in `through`. kind = "tunnel" (winding passages, the default, threshold around 0.1) or "cavern" (blobs, where noise is above the threshold). `scale` is how stretched the noise is (0.05), `squash` stretches it up and down.

name: nova.voxel.create_chunk
doc: Makes an empty chunk (chunk numbers: x and z divided by 16, rounded down).

name: nova.voxel.finish_chunk
doc: Works out the light of a chunk you have filled with `set`, `fill` and `carve`. It is drawn once it and the eight chunks around it are finished.

name: nova.voxel.has_chunk
doc: Whether the chunk is loaded.

name: nova.voxel.unload_chunk
doc: Forgets a chunk and its picture. Save its edits first.

name: nova.voxel.export_edits
doc: What the player changed in a chunk (by `edit`) as short text to put in a save, or nothing when it is untouched.

name: nova.voxel.import_edits
doc: Puts saved changes back into a chunk after generating it and before `finish_chunk`.

name: nova.voxel.modified_chunks
doc: The loaded chunks that have changes to save.

name: nova.voxel.light
doc: The light at a place, 0 to 15, from the sky and from torches.

name: nova.voxel.top
doc: The height of the highest full block in a column (-1 when there is none).

name: nova.voxel.raycast
signature: nova.voxel.raycast(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, length [, liquids]) -> bx, by, bz, nx, ny, nz, distance, block | nothing
doc: A ray through the blocks: the first block that is not air (or water, unless `liquids`), the way the face it hit points (nx, ny, nz: to place a block beside it, add that), how far away it was and what it is. Nothing when it hits nothing.

name: nova.voxel.move
signature: nova.voxel.move(x, y, z, half_width, height, dx, dy, dz [, step]) -> x, y, z, hit_x, hit_y, hit_z, on_ground
doc: Moves a standing box (feet at x, y, z) by dx, dy, dz and slides it along the blocks, so a body walks, falls, lands and bumps its head. `step` is how high it climbs without jumping (0.5 is a stair). It says which axes were blocked and whether it is standing on something.

name: nova.voxel.daylight
doc: How bright the sky's light is, 0 (night) to 1 (noon). Torch light is not affected. Set the sky and fog colours yourself.

name: nova.voxel.draw
doc: Draws the world around the camera: `distance` chunks out (6). Chunks are built in pieces 16 blocks high, on worker threads where the device has cores to spare: it hands the nearest pieces that changed to the workers, takes in at most `budget` finished pieces this frame (6) so that the frame rate holds, and without workers builds that many itself. Call it after nova.camera. A piece of the world that has only just been made fades in over `fade` seconds (0.4; 0 for none) by a screen-door, and the last tenth of `distance` fades out, so the world does not pop into view; a piece rebuilt by an edit does not fade again.

name: nova.voxel.cube
signature: nova.voxel.cube(block, x, y, z [, { scale, rx, ry, rz, tint }])
doc: Draws one block as a small cube centred on a place: a dropped item, a block in the hand.

name: nova.voxel.stats
signature: nova.voxel.stats() -> { chunks, meshed, mesh_ms, light_ms, faces, drawn, dirty, threads }
doc: What the voxel world is doing: chunks loaded, pieces built so far and the milliseconds the builders spent (added up over all threads) and the lighting, faces in the last piece, pieces drawn this frame, pieces waiting or being built, and how many worker threads build.

name: nova.clock
doc: A stopwatch that runs in real time (nova.time is game time, which stops when paused). For measuring how long work took, or spending a fixed share of a frame on it: `local t = nova.clock(); while nova.clock() - t < 0.004 do ... end`.

name: nova.voxel.apply_saved
doc: Puts back the changes the player made to this chunk before it was dropped, or that were read by `load_world`. Call it after generating a chunk and before `finish_chunk`.

name: nova.voxel.save_world
